identityReview: American movement organiser Alicia Garza, distinct from same-name softball players and accounting professionals in search results. Exact birth date is supported by the read museum biography and corroborated by the indexed HistoryMakers biography, whose direct page and finding-aid PDF returned 403. Birthplace disagreement is left unresolved and omitted. Do not conflate founding BLM with managing every organisation using the name.
lifeStatusEvidence: MIT’s retrospective confirms an actual keynote on 19 May 2026. Robinson’s 23 July 2026 NewsOne article reports a completed conversation with Garza; it provides later published activity evidence but no exact recording date. Neither a future event announcement nor the absence of a death record is used as proof of appearance. No audiovisual inspection is claimed.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read museum biography, university alumni section and lecture retrospectives, first-person AAIHS interview, Black Futures Lab organisational pages, JPB appointment release and renamed-foundation history, publisher edition metadata, Supermajority founding history and current primary transition announcement, award organiser’s ceremony record, and a participant-authored programme account. Read Commons license metadata.
corrections: Read National Women’s History Museum biography: explicit 4 January 1981 birth date, co-founding history and organising work. The birthplace Oakland conflicts with The HistoryMakers indexed biography’s Los Angeles and EBSCO overview’s Marin County; birthplace is omitted, not silently resolved. Avoid adopting charged descriptions of the Martin and Brown cases as findings of criminal guilt.

Read UC San Diego April 2018 alumni profile, specifically Garza’s section: graduation in 2002 in anthropology and sociology. Daniel Caspi’s adjacent Caltech PhD and medical patent are unrelated. The National Domestic Workers Alliance role is historical as of 2018. A claimed 2017 master’s degree lacked a directly verified university record in this review and is not asserted.

Read Garza’s interview published by AAIHS on 17 February 2020. Her own account distinguishes leaving BLM Global Network daily operations in 2017 from launching Black Futures Lab in 2018. Community surveys, organiser training and policy participation are described as its work. Tentative book title in the introduction is not the final title; numeric programme claims and future ambitions are not carried forward as current outcomes.

Read Black Futures Lab’s Who We Are page. It identifies Garza as founder and distinguishes the Lab, BLM Global Network and Movement for Black Lives coalition. Its Black Census Project is an organisational survey, not a federal enumeration. The current homepage also calls her founder and describes a 2026 response target; the target is not a completed count or evidence that she still directs daily operations.

Read original JPB Foundation appointment release dated 6 February 2024. It names Garza among six senior staff additions with the title Senior Vice President of Movement Infrastructure and Explorations. The date is an announcement, not a proven first working day. Bhargava’s presidency, board appointments and foundation-wide grant commitments do not belong to Garza personally.

Read Freedom Together foundation history: JPB was renamed in 2024, so these are successive names of the same foundation, not two separate employers. Its presidential succession is not Garza’s job history. No foundation grant totals are treated as her personal assets or donations.

Read publisher edition metadata and description: ebook and audiobook dated 20 October 2020; paperback 7 September 2021. Do not substitute the paperback date for original publication or carry the older tentative title forward. Promotional endorsements and bestseller labels are not used as independent evaluations.

Read Supermajority’s Our Story: 2019 launch with Cecile Richards, Ai-jen Poo and Garza; the related education fund has additional founding collaborators. Use nonexclusive co-founder language and do not confuse these organisational structures. Undated membership totals and stale active-status copy are superseded by its 2026 announcement.

Read Supermajority’s primary announcement dated 8 January 2026. It states that the organisation will no longer remain standalone and directs members toward local organising and groups including the ACLU. This is not proof of a legal merger, acquisition or insolvency. Do not treat the claim of 20 million voters activated as an independently audited effect or attribute organisational closure to personal misconduct.

Read Sydney Peace Foundation’s 2017 recipient and ceremony account. The laureate was the Black Lives Matter Global Network. On 2 November, Patrisse Cullors, Rodney Diverlus and Dawn Modkins accepted on its behalf. Do not claim Garza personally attended or alone received the prize, notwithstanding compressed secondary biographies.

Read MIT Picower Institute’s retrospective published 2 June 2026 describing the actual 19 May symposium. It identifies Garza as Freedom Together senior vice president and describes her keynote, The Politics of Hope. The event and publication dates differ; 300 registrations are not a verified attendance total. Her views on hope are attributed speech, not a neuroscience finding of her own.

Read Rashad Robinson’s NewsOne article published 23 July 2026. It describes a completed Freedom Table conversation in which Garza guest-hosted Robinson and LaTosha Brown. Exact recording date was not stated; July 23 is publication, not an asserted date of physical appearance. From Presence to Power is Robinson’s book, not Garza’s. No video or audio inspection is claimed.

Read Yale Law School’s account of Garza’s 4 March 2024 lecture: National Domestic Workers Alliance special-projects role from 2013 and transition to the JPB Foundation. This corroborates that the February announcement did not mean all prior roles ended that day. The page’s differing Global Justice/Women’s Rights headings are not treated as two events. No law degree or Yale appointment is inferred.

Preserve appointment announcement versus transition, founder versus daily manager, foundation renaming, community survey versus government census, publication versus recording dates, book edition dates and network award versus personal attendance.
